title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Service Operations Agent for conversational admin setup
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, billing requirements, administrator roles and billing controls are supported. The updated consumption-billing guidance still supports prepaid capacity alongside pay-as-you-go. Minor corrections remain for an uncited supporting page and checklist controls not represented in the table.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Refresh the MCP connection by selecting the environment in Power Apps, opening Connections, deleting D365 Contact Center MCP Connection and recreating it through a new Admin Copilot conversation.
claims.quote: Select the correct environment in the upper-right corner. Select Connections in the left pane. Locate D365 Contact Center MCP Connection, and then delete it. In Copilot Service admin center, open Admin Copilot, and then start a new conversation.

claims.claim: Removing the environment from the billing plan stops further pay-as-you-go charges for that environment.
claims.quote: the environment ceases to be pay-as-you-go and goes back to functioning as a regular environment. Any usage that was already incurred up to this point is billed to your Azure subscription, but no further usage is charged.

claims.claim: Environment admins can create billing plans, with editing and linking restricted to their own plans and environments.
claims.quote: Environment admin | Yes | Yes, for billing policies the admin created. | Yes, for billing policies the admin created and for environments in which they're admins.

claims.claim: Power Platform admins can create billing plans and edit or link environments tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin | Yes | Yes, for all billing policies in the tenant. | Yes, for all environments in the tenant.

claims.claim: Global admins can create billing plans and edit or link environments tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Global admin | Yes | Yes, for all billing policies in the tenant. | Yes, for all environments in the tenant.

claims.claim: Dynamics 365 admins can create billing plans and edit or link environments tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 admin | Yes | Yes, for all billing policies in the tenant. | Yes, for all environments in the tenant.

claims.claim: The consumption-billing page does not specify how removing pay-as-you-go affects Service Operations Agent.
claims.quote: Searched: "Service Operations Agent" "Conversational Setup" credits price billing; "Service Operations Agent" disable turn off Power Platform API Dataverse setting. Opened setup-pay-as-you-go, pay-as-you-go-set-up and the feature page. No agent-specific consequence of unlinking billing is stated.

claims.claim: The Service Operations Agent page does not state whether Quality Assurance Agent or Customer Assist Agent shares its meter or prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: "Service Operations Agent" "Customer Assist" billing prerequisites. Opened Use Service Operations Agent and overview-contact-center-agents; reviewed returned billing and Customer Assist passages. The Service Operations Agent page gives no shared-meter or shared-prerequisite statement.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to check role assignments, Application Insights, the MCP connection and Cost Management budgets, but the table has no corresponding rows.
claims.quote: Identify who holds the Omnichannel administrator and System Administrator roles; Connect Application Insights; Review usage and budgets; Recheck the role holders and the connection. Table: billing-plan membership and an undocumented feature-off switch only.
claims.fix: Add after the table: 'The checklist also covers role assignments, the Application Insights connection, the MCP connection and Microsoft Cost Management budgets; those controls are not represented in this table.' Do not add rows in this correction.

claims.claim: Dataverse security role assignments govern users' access and privileges.
claims.quote: Security roles define how different users access different types of records. To control access to data and resources, you can create or modify security roles and change the security roles that are assigned to users.

claims.claim: Microsoft's responsible AI FAQ recommends reviewing and verifying configuration changes, particularly in production.
claims.quote: Organizations should maintain review and verification steps for setup and configuration changes, particularly in production environments, and use manual administration paths when the system indicates uncertainty or when a scenario falls outside supported workflows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises clear prompts specifying relevant configuration context.
claims.quote: administrators should provide clear and specific prompts, include relevant context such as queue names or channel types, review responses before applying changes, and verify configuration outcomes in the admin experience.

claims.claim: The feature page does not describe refreshing or deleting its MCP connection as a way to block the agent.
claims.quote: Searched: "Service Operations Agent" "MCP" "disable". Opened Use Service Operations Agent and data-platform-mcp-disable. The feature page documents deleting and recreating the connection only to configure or refresh it, not as an off switch.
